26.title: Acts Prohibited in Reserved Forests
26.details: Federally active. Penalties significantly enhanced under KP Forest Ordinance 2002. Covers unauthorized tree felling, starting fires, and clearing land in reserved forest.
26.penalty: Historical: 6 months or Rs. 500. Enhanced under KPK Ordinance 2002: Up to 2 years / Rs. 50,000.
26.amendments: KPK Forest Ordinance, 2002 (Section 4); NWFP (Amendment) Act, 2006; Punjab Forest (Amendment) Act, 2010.

33.title: Acts Prohibited in Protected Forests
33.details: Regulates felling and quarrying in protected domains without explicit authorization from the DFO.
33.penalty: Up to 6 months imprisonment / Rs. 500 fine historically. Enhanced locally under KPK Ordinance 2002.
33.amendments: KPK Forest Ordinance, 2002 extended protections to community-managed forests.

34.title: Power to Issue Rules for Protected Forests
34.details: Empowers provincial governments to regulate grazing, movement of cattle, and removal of forest produce from protected forests.
34.penalty: Violation of rules: Fine up to Rs. 500 or 6 months imprisonment.
34.amendments: Powers delegated to DFOs under provincial devolution orders post-18th Amendment.
case_references: 2020 MLD 1622 (Provincial Government KPK v. Zaman Khan)

52.title: Seizure of Property Liable to Confiscation
52.details: Vests extreme power to Forest Officers to seize tools, vehicles, and timber involved in suspected forestry offences without a magistrate's warrant.
52.penalty: Instrument expropriation / Vehicle impoundment. Increasingly non-releasable via standard bail.
52.amendments: KPK High Court directives (2019-2023) have progressively restricted bail for seized vehicles under this section.

68.title: Power to Compound Offences
68.details: Forest Officers of Division rank or above may compound (settle out of court) any forest offence, accepting compensation in lieu of prosecution.
68.penalty: Compensation amount determined by officer based on damage assessment and timber value.
68.amendments: Compounding authority now requires approval of Conservator for offences exceeding Rs. 100,000 under KPK rules.

69.title: Presumption that Forest Produce Belongs to Government
69.details: Whenever a question arises as to whether any forest-produce is the property of the Government, such produce shall be presumed to be the property of the Government until the contrary is proved.
69.penalty: N/A (Evidentiary Rule). Reverses the burden of proof onto the accused.
69.amendments: Strictly upheld by the Supreme Court of Pakistan across multiple constitutional petitions.
case_references: 2022 PLD 95 (Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Forest Dept v. Rehman Gul)

73.title: Power to Make Rules
73.details: Provincial government's overarching rule-making authority for regulating transit of timber, licensing of sawmills, and forest management plans.
73.penalty: Violation of rules: Punishable under Section 26 or Section 33 depending on forest classification.
73.amendments: Post-18th Amendment (2010), all rule-making authority devolved to provincial legislatures.

100.title: Repeal of Minor Conflicting Provisions
100.details: The exact wording of historical minor fines under the 1927 Act was formally overridden in KP by this ordinance. Replaced by enhanced penalty schedules.
100.amendments: Superseded by KPK Forest Ordinance, 2002, Sections 3-8.
